question: Which channelizing device in Figure 6K-1 is illustrated with three horizontal striped rails?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The channelizing device shown in Figure 6K-1 with three horizontal, diagonally striped rails is the Type 3 Barricade. In the figure, it is depicted with three stacked rails (each 8 to 12 inches tall, striped at 45 degrees), a minimum overall height of 5 feet, and a minimum rail length of 4 feet. By comparison, the Type 1 Barricade has one rail and the Type 2 Barricade has two rails. Standards (mandatory): - "Designs of various channelizing devices shall be as shown in Figure 6K-1. All channelizing devices shall be crashworthy (see definition in Section 1C.02)." - For distinction, the Direction Indicator Barricade is a different device: "The Direction Indicator Barricade (see Figure 6K-1) shall consist of a One-Direction Large Arrow (W1-6) sign mounted above a diagonal striped, horizontally-aligned, retroreflective rail." (a single rail beneath an arrow sign, not three rails). Visual evidence: - [Image 2] shows Figure 6K-1, in which the "TYPE 3 BARRICADE" is drawn with three horizontal striped rails at a 45° stripe angle, 8 to 12 inches high each, a 5 ft minimum overall height, and 4 ft minimum rail length, whereas the Type 1 and Type 2 Barricades show one and two rails respectively. - [Image 1] is the referenced Figure 6K-1 caption confirming that channelizing device designs shall be as shown in that figure. Citations: - Section 6K.01 Standard §1 (p.815) - Section 6K.08 Standard §1 (p.821) - Figure 6K-1 (p.815) - Page 857
